messages.content: Thanks—yeah, I put the perlite mix together yesterday, and the texture’s way better. Drains fast but still holds a bit of moisture. Two cuttings are already showing tiny roots after just four days, which is way quicker than last time. Might’ve cracked the code, or I just got lucky. Either way, I’ll pot one up this weekend and see how it handles real soil. Fingers crossed.
That’s excellent news on the root development—seeing results that quickly is a great sign! Good luck with the potting this weekend; I'd love to hear how the soil holds up against the new mix!

Turns out the first potted one’s doing fine—soil’s not drying too fast, and no droop yet. I kept it shaded like I always do, but honestly, it’s looking stronger than anything I’ve had survive past week two. Might finally have a system that works. Now I’m tempted to try grafting one of the hardier shoots onto a rootstock next month. Risky, but if the base holds, it could change everything out here.

That's a huge win—getting consistent growth after a rough week is a huge step! That "hardier shoot" idea is interesting—if the base is stable, that could be the game-changer you’re looking for. Let me know how the rootstock experiment goes; I'm keen to hear if it's as successful as you're hoping for!

Appreciate that—it’s small, but feels like momentum. I labeled the grafted one “gamble” just to keep myself honest. If it makes it two weeks, I’ll consider tweaking the support stakes—current ones are splintering with the wind. Still relying on borrowed tools for the build next week, though. Delivery’s late *again*, so I’m scrambling to rearrange the schedule. Not ideal, but we’ll make it work.

result.content: "Gamble" - what a unique name for a project! It sounds like you’re really finding your groove with this new mix. Hopefully, the rest of your schedule adjusts smoothly, and I hope that new rootstock experiment pays off; a successful grafting would be a big breakthrough! Keep me updated on how those "gambles" turn out!
